hana: hey team, just started today. trying to get a single dev setup across python/node/go/rust on an Intel MBA. asdf python keeps failing with "openssl not found" during compilation. any quick wins?

devex: welcome hana! :wave: quick wins: brew install openssl@1.1 and pkg-config, then export LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS/PKG_CONFIG_PATH to point at /usr/local/opt/openssl@1.1. also ensure Xcode command line tools installed (`xcode-select --install`).

kevin: echoing that. for Intel macs brew prefix is /usr/local. snippet that helped me: 
```bash
brew install openssl@1.1 pkg-config
export LDFLAGS="-L/usr/local/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/usr/local/opt/openssl@1.1/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/usr/local/opt/openssl@1.1/lib/pkgconfig"
asdf plugin-add python || true
asdf install python 3.11.5
```

hana: thanks! curious about dotfiles strategy here. do folks keep global .tool-versions or per-repo?

luca: per-repo is preferred. for personal machine i keep a local-only `~/.tool-versions-personal` in dotfiles and symlink it. avoid committing personal pins.

devex: also remember nodejs plugin needs gpg to verify. `brew install gpg` then follow asdf-nodejs docs to import keys. for yarn we use corepack: `corepack enable` after installing node.

hana: ssh/gpg for commit signing and remote agent forwarding?

kevin: on mac: generate ed25519 key, add to github, use `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain`. ssh config: AddKeysToAgent yes, UseKeychain yes, ForwardAgent yes. For signing, generate a GPG key and set `git config --global user.signingkey <keyid>` and `git config --global commit.gpgsign true`.

setup-bot: reminder: request access to "Redwood - Developer Secrets" 1Password vault.

hana: ok installed openssl and python build worked. next up node + go. thanks all!
